pages.transcription:
26. Oktober

Dear Manfred & Hannah, this only to tell you that we are
safely arrived in Buenos. Lotte was sufficiently exhausted
and we cant open 2 flower-shops with the flowers we found
in our apartement here. Then we went straight away {leerry}
behind all the people in the hall/ to the Opera where we had tickets for a
marvellous ballet and now I have to pay for all that with lectures in all
languages. The English, the Spanish are well arranged, but the great difficul[?]
by all the Jews. There are 250000 in this town and I have promised a
lecture for charity-purposes - now they fight, who shall arrange the lecture,
the Zionist, the refugees, the Spanioles and I have the secret hope, that
by this quarrel I shall escape, because they will not have finished the
discussions during my stay here. We go also to Cordoba, Rosario and
after that to Montevideo. The seven hours in the plane were a bit
shaky but we arrived without any trouble except that in the {20 minutes}
stay at Porto Alegre I could not get a coffee and smoke a cigare
because we had there a reception. In these countries a foreign writer
is still a rare and appreciated beast and the curiosity takes much of
our time, poor Lotte is hanging constantly on the phone and ex-
plaining in five different languages that we do not accept invitations.
All this will be over in a fortnight and then I am finally well a
month or six weeks before going for Newyork. We have no news
from Eva who will is not like to become ever a great writer but
I knew through my sister in law that she is happy and I wish
you could be with her. We speak every day how I regret it is that
you have to support all the difficulties - dont believe that we forget
you. For Freivental I have already tried something but it will
take some time. And poor Planker, - one cannot help him but we -
terially. Kindest regards to all from yours
Stefan Zweig
pages.notes: Brief auf Hotelpapier (City Hotel, Buenos Aires). Handschrift in violetter Tinte. Die Zeile 'behind all the people in the hall/' ist leicht durchgestrichen, aber lesbar.

result.confidence_notes: Der Text ist sehr gut lesbar, trotz der kursiven Handschrift. Einzelne Wörter wie 'difficul[?]' sind aufgrund des Zeilenendes oder der Tintenführung leicht unsicher, aber im Kontext eindeutig.
